Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

precmed (development version)

Major changes

  • Added a population-level cumulative hazard ratio at tau0 to survival atefit() output. It uses the same outcome, propensity-score and censoring models as the RMST analysis, with bootstrap inference. The new log.cumulative.hazard.ratio is distinct from the existing conditional Cox log.hazard.ratio and is included in printing, plotting, coef() and confint(). Inference is unavailable if the estimate or any bootstrap replicate is undefined.

  • Replaced the gbm dependency with gbm3 for boosting models across count, survival, and internal continuous-outcome methods. Existing tuning argument names and the learning rate of 0.1 are preserved, rather than adopting the GBM3 learning-rate default of 0.001. Parallel controls map to GBM3 threads. Stored boosting fits now have class GBMFit. Results can differ from gbm even with identical settings and random seeds because random-number usage and Poisson updates for zero-event leaves differ between the packages.

  • Fixed continuous boosting predictions by retaining the selected tree count for each treatment arm, and forwarding additional boosting controls.

  • Added C backends, enabled by default, for count and survival contrast regression, Cox restricted mean survival integration, and LASSO propensity-score interaction screening. Installing from source now requires a C compiler and R’s standard BLAS/LAPACK libraries.

  • Added contrast.control, rmst.control, and ps.control to select numerical backends independently of model-fitting arguments. Set solver = "R" in the relevant list to use the R implementation. contrast.control also accepts Newton-Raphson settings and nested optim.control options for fallback optimization. Small floating-point differences between backends are possible.

Minor changes and bug fixes

  • Use GBM3 cross-validation for single-predictor count boosting fits and boosting initial predictions, removing the legacy out-of-bag workaround and fixing a cross-fitting error when selecting the number of trees.

  • Return NA with an informative warning for count-outcome responder subgroups missing one or both treatment arms, instead of failing the analysis. ABC is NA when a required validation estimate is unavailable.

  • Fixed survival Cox hazard ratios to censor follow-up at tau0 instead of treating observations beyond the horizon as events. This affects ATE, subgroup, and cross-validation hazard ratio estimates; RMST and RMTL calculations are unchanged.

  • Fixed survival random forest event coding at tau0 and integrated predicted survival curves through the full horizon when computing RMST. Survival forest scores and scores using forest initial predictions may change.

  • Warn when an out-of-range doubly robust RMST estimate is replaced by an outcome-model estimate, including when this occurs during bootstrap inference.

  • Fixed intercept-only propensity models in survival cross-fitting, subgroup evaluation, and bootstrap ATE estimation by preserving matrix dimensions.

  • Fixed LASSO propensity-score dimension handling with two predictors or a single prediction row.

  • Reused model designs and GLM families during count and continuous-outcome balanced splitting to avoid repeated formula processing. Continuous-outcome public APIs remain disabled as before.

  • Used lm.fit() for complete-data continuous contrast regression and reused the slope generalized inverse in the sandwich covariance, preserving coefficient labels and the formula path for incomplete inputs.

  • Accelerated Breslow censoring probabilities using cumulative hazards and interval lookup instead of repeated scans and sums.

  • Reused the full-data fit returned by cv.glmnet() instead of fitting the same propensity-score LASSO path separately.

  • Removed a duplicate treated-arm boosting fit in count cross-fitting. Results obtained with the same seed may change because fewer random draws are consumed.

  • Updated validation plots and box plots for current ggplot2 and tidyselect versions; ggplot2 >= 3.4.0 is now required.

  • Added the book chapter by Jiang et al. (2026) to the package description and references.

  • Added Smart Data Analysis and Statistics B.V. as copyright holder for its contributions after version 1.1.0, alongside the existing Biogen attribution.

precmed 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2024-10-05

  • Removed dependency on the MESS package.
  • Fixed an issue in the cross-validation procedure that lead to an increased total sample size
  • Updated documentation using roxygen2 (version 7.3.2) and resolved bracketing issues.

precmed 1.0.0.9000

  • Added a NEWS.md file to track changes to the package.
